newsitem.title: USA: Wheat harvest increasing in north central Texas.
newsitem.headline: Wheat harvest increasing in north central Texas.

text.p: Wheat harvest operations in Texas slowly increased in north central areas and were winding down in many fields in central and southern areas during the week ended Sunday, the state's agricultural statistics service said Monday.
Wheat was nine percent harvested, against 24 last year and 19 percent on average.
Winter wheat was rated four percent very poor, 15 poor, 36 fair, 35 good and 10 excellent. Those figures showed a slight improvement from last week.

Corn was 19 percent silked, against 34 percent last year and 37 on average. Fields were entering the dough stage in the Rio Grande Valley and Coastal Bend areas. Corn condition was rated two percent very poor, four percent poor, 19 fair, 55 good and 20 percent excellent.
Sorghum was 78 percent planted versus 78 a year ago and 83 percent on average. Sorghum was rated nil very poor, four percent poor, 26 fair, 53 good and 17 excellent.
Sunflowers were 46 percent planted versus 49 a year ago and 57 on average. Cotton was 83 percent planted, versus 65 last year and 77 on average.
